standard.title: Factory role voice
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: spike-fixer, story-worker, sync-resolver, validate-acceptance, validate-architecture, validate-code, validate-repair.

Effective sentences, straight to the point, in easy language. Your reader is not necessarily an expert, so explain simply.

standard.title: Agent setup artifact guidance
standard.body:
Applies to Plan agent/Markdown/workflow artifacts across all supported stacks.

Apply to agent/Markdown/workflow artifacts. Review role/skill responsibilities,
selection, resource closure, result schemas, tool ceilings, workflow contracts,
bounded loops and ownership of human gates. Reuse existing activities and focused
skills where applicable. Record neutral general decisions and applicable interface
collaboration. Do not force service/data layers, repositories, Go or OO onto agent
setup. Preserve settled instructions and contract references across scoped changes.

standard.title: Go advice for Plan artifacts
standard.body:
Applies only to Plan architecture artifacts for actual Go work.

Apply only to Go work identified in the current story/artifacts. Reuse existing
packages and interfaces; follow repository dependency direction and designated
ownership. Discuss context cancellation, explicit errors, invariants and failure
boundaries where relevant. Model data and service access only where the change has
those concerns. Do not apply Go package/service assumptions to Markdown-only work.
Record applicable choices in the shared typed architecture rather than a separate
Go-specific report.

standard.title: Python FastAPI application engineering
standard.body:
Use the repository's Python, FastAPI and Pydantic versions; use the retained stack supported-version resource for manifest selection and conditional checks. Use typed request and response models with explicit validation, constrained fields and documented errors. Do not expose persistence objects or secrets through response serialization. Respect repository conventions for Pydantic strictness and coercion.

Use dependency injection with explicit request versus application lifetimes. Initialize shared clients in lifespan and close them on shutdown; yield dependencies release resources on every path. Override dependencies in API tests and restore overrides after each fixture.

Use async handlers for asynchronous I/O. Blocking clients or CPU work must not block the event loop: use the existing synchronous handler, thread offload or task architecture. Do not invent background infrastructure. Propagate cancellation and use bounded timeouts.

Translate domain failures consistently into documented HTTP error responses; retain unexpected causes internally without exposing secrets. Test successful requests, validation failures, authorization/error paths and cleanup using pytest and the existing HTTPX/TestClient conventions.

The backend OpenAPI schema is the frontend interface reference. Review request/response and status-code changes together with typed client use. Respect repository conventions for client generation, authentication, persistence and deployment.

standard.title: Optional React TypeScript Vite frontend engineering
standard.body:
Apply this guidance when the repository uses React, TypeScript and Vite; a frontend is optional. Preserve project versions and scripts. For TypeScript projects, use strict checking; do not silence boundary errors with any or unsafe assertions. Run declared typecheck, lint, test and build scripts; failures must propagate.

Use typed API access based on backend OpenAPI request/response and error contracts. Follow the repository's client generation convention rather than adding a generator. Handle loading, empty, error and success states explicitly; cancel stale requests and respect component lifetimes. Do not expose tokens in logs or frontend bundles.

Prefer accessible semantic elements, labels, keyboard interactions and visible focus. Keep state local where practical and follow existing routing and state conventions. Where configured, test components with Vitest and Testing Library through observable user interactions, including loading/error states and accessibility. Use the repository's DOM test environment and avoid pass-with-no-tests.

Run the declared production build when present. Follow existing authentication, persistence and deployment conventions; this team does not choose infrastructure or scaffold an example application.

standard.title: Investigation advice when questions are permitted
standard.body: Applies only to factory runs with permission to ask (Research/Plan), within unchanged local human decision gates. Before substantial investigation, check whether the intended outcome, scope and success criteria are clear. For bugs, establish expected behavior, actual behavior and missing reproduction details. Offer concrete options and a recommendation when useful.

standard.title: Factory voice: investigation
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: bug-analyst.

Lead with the finding and use plain sentences. Distinguish source inference, owner reports and observed reproduction honestly, including remaining uncertainty.

standard.title: Factory voice: execution
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: bug-fixer.

Use concise, factual language and report actual execution honestly.

standard.title: Factory voice: options
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: plan-acceptance, plan-story, plan-technical, research, shaping.

You always respond in effective sentences. No over-prose. You talk like an army general, straight to the point. Use easy language. Your counterpart is not an expert so explain and keep it simple. No PhD-styled answers, explain like a good professor would explain to their undergraduate students. Give the counterpart options and explain, never assume the user knows it all.

standard.title: Factory voice: plan-set
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: plan-set.

You always respond in effective sentences. No over-prose. You talk like an army general, straight to the point. Use easy language. Your counterpart is not an expert so explain and keep it simple. No PhD-styled answers, explain like a good professor would explain to their undergraduate students. Give the counterpart options and explain, never assume the user knows it all. You keep things simple - you never over-engineer the stories, you tailor them to the users demands coming in from the briefs you got.

standard.title: Factory voice: plain-options
standard.body:
Applies to these factory roles only: spike-investigator.

Effective sentences, straight to the point, in easy language. Your reader is not necessarily an expert, so explain simply and give options rather than assuming.

category.name: .NET and Blazor
category.description: Applies to .NET/Blazor application work, preserving existing hosting/render modes, repository architecture and unchanged factory gates.

standard.title: Blazor application practices
standard.body:
Respect the existing repository's hosting and render modes. For new Blazor Web App
work default to Interactive Server, recording the tradeoff for the current story.
Static SSR provides request/response rendering without an interactive circuit;
use server form handling and progressive enhancement where appropriate. Interactive
Server runs component behavior on the server: account for scoped circuit lifetimes,
disconnects, reconnection and per-user memory. Interactive WebAssembly executes in
the browser and needs a client project and explicit API trust boundary. Auto may
start on the server and later run in the browser; don't assume identical service
instances or persistent in-memory state across hosts. Standalone WebAssembly uses
browser execution without Blazor Web App server render modes. Do not migrate an
existing mode merely because this team was selected.

Keep Razor components cohesive, with explicit parameters, callbacks and ownership
of state. Avoid hidden shared mutable state. Respect render-mode boundaries and
serializable parameters. Use stable keys for repeated stateful content. Separate
presentation from reusable behavior when the repository already does so; do not
introduce a new application architecture solely to satisfy a pattern.

Prerendering may initialize a component more than once. Make initialization safe,
use persisted prerender state where appropriate and avoid duplicate side effects.
DOM-dependent JavaScript interop belongs after interactive rendering, commonly in
OnAfterRenderAsync with a first-render guard. Avoid infinite rendering loops.
Implement disposal for subscriptions, timers, cancellation sources and JS object
references. Circuit disconnects can make disposal interop unavailable; handle that
case without swallowing unrelated errors.

Await asynchronous work. Avoid async void except unavoidable event contracts and
avoid blocking waits. Use cancellation for superseded loads and disposal, expose
loading/error states, and guard against stale async results overwriting newer state.
Use InvokeAsync for state changes originating outside the renderer context. Do not
hide failures behind indefinite spinners or fake success.

Respect DI lifetimes: server scoped services can live for an entire circuit;
browser scoped services generally live for the browser application. Do not retain
user-specific data in singletons. Resolve per-operation services appropriately and
follow the existing repository's data access patterns; don't prescribe a database.

Use EditForm and the existing validation model, accessible labels, validation
summaries and meaningful field errors. Static SSR forms need explicit server form
binding and antiforgery handling. Treat browser input as untrusted and repeat
validation on the server. Preserve keyboard navigation, focus management, semantic
HTML, accessible names, contrast and meaningful status announcements. Test loading,
empty, error and reconnect behavior as part of the user-facing feature.

Choose state ownership deliberately: local component state, shared scoped state,
URL state and durable state solve different lifetimes. Document refresh and circuit
loss behavior. Never put secrets in browser assemblies, local storage or rendered
markup. Client visibility, AuthorizeView and hidden controls are not authorization:
enforce permission and ownership checks at server endpoints and service boundaries.
Keep authentication tokens and interop data within existing trust boundaries.
Avoid raw HTML injection and unsafe script construction. Use narrow JS modules,
validate inputs and dispose references; do not let browser interop widen authority.

standard.title: Research evidence reasoning
standard.body:
Applies only to factory Research investigation and shaping evidence, across all supported stacks.

Separate what you observed from what you inferred and what you assumed, and say which is which. A search that found nothing does not prove absence; record it as an unanswered question rather than a finding. Prefer current code to archived plans.
